shots.text:
Before the world, there was only the sea. Fire and water. Stone and storm. Root, and starless dark.

All of it one. And nothing.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Black. Slowly, a churning sea of every colour at once, no horizon, colours bleeding into each other.

shots.text:
Seven stepped out of it. Six were content to be one thing each.

The seventh wanted to be everything.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Seven tall silhouettes rise from the sea in a line, each glowing one colour (red, blue-white, green, teal, ochre, violet). The seventh is a black outline with no colour at all.

shots.text:
His name was Vael-Orrun. Where he walked, the elements did not mix.

They stopped.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: The black figure walks forward. Around his feet the colours of the sea freeze into grey glass. Behind him the sky shows a black sun with a crown-shaped gap in its corona.

shots.text:
The Six could not kill him. So they joined hands, each across from its opposite, and drove him out past the edge of the stars.

We call it the Ring.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Top-down: the six coloured figures in a ring, Fire across from Water, Storm across from Earth, Nature across from Void, hands joined. The black figure is flung out through the edge of a starfield. The six lights settle into six lands around a centre.

shots.text:
At its heart, six peoples built Solenne. The Crowned Heart.

My city.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Dawn over Solenne: six concentric white walls each faced with a different stone, the Heartstone glowing in the open hall at the centre, the golden Sunstone lens hanging in the sky above.

shots.text: Six years ago, a man I loved like a father lost his daughter to the dark. Something beyond the stars made him a promise.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Night. Cassivane Dral, the Lord Marshal, alone on a balcony, holding a gold locket. Over his shoulder, in the stars, the faint crown-shaped gap. His face is in shadow.

shots.text: On the night of the Black Comet, the edge of the world split open.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: The Hollow Rift: violet grass, a ring of black pillars singing with stolen light. A black comet crosses the sky. The ground at the centre tears open into a crack full of nothing.

shots.text: Oswin, the Grey Lantern, held it for one night. At dawn, he walked to the edge... and gave it every light he had.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Oswin, old, grey robes and hat, walks to the lip of the Crack with his lantern-staff raised. Behind him a line of Spirewright towers burning in six colours. Grey shapes crawling out of the Crack.

shots.text:
The Crack closed to a hairline.

And Oswin fell. His lantern went out.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: A blast of white light; the Crack slams almost shut. The ground under Oswin gives way. He falls into the dark, the lantern going out. Last frame: one tiny spark still drifting down after him.

shots.text: But a voice can pass through a hairline. It drove the six sleeping Wardens mad, and now each land marches on the one across from it.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Six quick cuts: a volcano burning grey, a stormcloud gone solid black, a giant tree rotting, a frozen sea heaving, a mountain opening grey eyes, a starless sky with a crown. Then hordes of grey-eyed elemental spirits pouring across the land toward each other.

shots.text:
We cannot win back the lands. We can only hold the roads until their people escape.

Every road we hold will cost us a city.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: A long line of refugees with carts on an ash road. Tamsin Reed with her lantern-pole waving them on. A gloved hand sets a glowing keystone into the foundation of a stone tower.

shots.text:
I am Ysolde, Queen of a city that is running out of cities. And you, Spirewright, are the last of Oswin's apprentices.

Hold the road.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Queen Ysolde on the white walls of Solenne, looking east toward smoke on the horizon. Title card.
